candidates.title: Count open and urgent support tickets

demandEvidence.chore: Count open support tickets and count which open tickets are urgent.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Build a native n8n workflow to count how many are open, then how many of those open tickets are urgent.

ease.reason: A beginner can test counts on supplied fictional rows; the n8n reference documents Count and Count Unique, but not ticket access or urgency rules.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: a support team might pay to summarize a queue, but this challenge supplies no buyer, repeated demand, or payment evidence.

feasibility.reason: A four-week fictional-row prototype can count open and operator-labeled urgent items; the reference supports aggregation only, not live integration or urgency classification.

autonomy.reason: A manual test run can calculate and report counts using the documented summarize operation; a person must supply rows, define urgency, and verify results.

evidence.reason: The discussion states the exact counting chore and n8n docs support aggregation, but neither establishes a customer, urgency logic, or production integration.

candidates.reason: Assessed a narrow fictional-row experiment: operator supplies ticket status and urgency labels, a manual run counts open rows and urgent open rows, then a person checks the result. The documented Summarize node supports counts, not urgency classification or live ticket access. Excluded as a duplicate workflow and customer of recent post 98b4f6281cc3de4ecdfa95f6, which covers support inbox handling for online shops/support teams; this is support-ticket queue triage for support teams. Equal-weight mean 5.2 is below threshold.

steps.message: Assessed all ten assigned discussion identities. The support-ticket counting task was scored against an attached n8n aggregation reference, then excluded as a duplicate of recent support-inbox workflow/customer 98b4f6281cc3de4ecdfa95f6 and below threshold (mean 5.2). The assigned Make debugging request received its five-criterion assessment and was excluded below threshold (mean 4.0). The other eight assignments lack a sufficiently concrete distinct chore; no post proposed.
